subject: Follow Up Questions
body:
Dear Amin,

Thanks for coming to Santa Barbara to show us the app! It was really informative and helpful for us in our process of launching our first experience sampling study.
 
We have a few follow-up questions/requests on topics we touched on at the meeting. Specifically, we would like to kindly ask for clarification on which of these requests can be incorporated as part of the app's basic features (at no additional cost) and which would require a custom modification. For the latter, it would be helpful to receive an estimated timeline and cost for implementation.
  1. Batch Image Downloading: As we discussed, the ability to batch download images is crucial for us, as it would allow us to download and check the images in a timely manner and create follow up tests using them. You mentioned the possibility of providing a web scraping script that could automate downloading photos from the CSV file links. We believe this feature would benefit not only us but other users as well, so we kindly ask if this could be added as a core feature of the app. We would appreciate making this a priority, as we want to test the script soon and incorporate it into our data processing pipeline.
  2. Autocorrect for Text Responses: We are interested in exploring the possibility of adding an autocorrect function for text-based response questions. Could you provide us with a quote for implementing this feature and an estimate of how long it might take to integrate?
  3. Clock Format Consistency: Mengsi noticed a potential issue with time-based data collection, where the responses were recorded in a 24-hour format despite her input being in a 12-hour AM/PM format (likely due to her phone’s settings). We would like the time data input and output to be formatted consistently, regardless of participants’ device settings to avoid confusion. Is this something that could be addressed?
  4. Text Formatting Options: Some of our questions include long descriptions, and while we don't want them displayed in full every time, we’d like participants to be able to access them easily when needed. Is there a way to create collapsible/foldable text, where the full description is revealed upon clicking? Additionally, could we customize font size, style, and color etc to improve readability and reduce participants' cognitive load? We believe these features will also be beneficial for other users!
  5. Metadata Labels: We noticed that some of the metadata output contains numeric values for e.g. status and unanswered IDs, which we were unable to identify during the meeting. Could you clarify what labels or information are associated with these numbers?
  6. FAQ Page: We briefly mentioned the creation of an FAQ page but didn’t get into specifics. Could you let us know what resources or tools are available to help us build this feature within the app?
  7. Annual Plan Quote: Finally, we would appreciate an updated quote for the annual plan if we aim to run approximately 60 participants and administer up to six surveys simultaneously.
That's all for now and please let us know if anything is unclear!

Best,
Nadu, Sydney and Mengsi

Amin Tavassolian jan AFAIK while we're able to implement a dictionary to detect errors (and a script to change them to the closest correct word) this is NOT recommended. Phone virtual keyboards all have Autocorrect features and they're much more capable as they can detect misclicks as well. The decision is up to you.
As for styling, I'm not sure if we support any mark-down on HTML formatting for our text but it's straightforward since we need them implemented for terms and conditions on mobile apps as well.
I would like to know more about their FAQ page and its extent.
The clock needs an update for iOS/Android and Web app FE. It's easy to implement but we need to thread carefully not to mess up the existing studies.

subject: Follow Up Questions
body:
Hi Sydney,

I hope you're doing well, and I apologize for the delay in my response.

I've discussed your inquiries with the team and have addressed each one below:
  1. Batch Image Downloading: We can provide you with an API to handle this quickly at no additional cost.

  3. Clock Format Consistency: We can address this matter in about two to three weeks, but it will require some custom configuration in the system.
  4. Text Formatting Options: This feature requires additional work on our end. We already have it in our pipeline and need to prioritize its completion, with delivery expected by early next year. Please let us know if this timeline works for you.

  7. Annual Plan Quote: Assuming you plan to conduct six studies over the year, each with up to 60 participants lasting about three months, we recommend a quota of 5,000 participant/week as a cost-efficient approach. The total cost for this annual subscription license to collect survey data will be USD 2,518. Should you choose this option, we will include the FAQ page at no additional charge.
As mentioned, items 3 and 4 will also require some customization on our end. We would be happy to implement them for a fee of USD 498. Please let us know your thoughts on the quotes provided, and we can proceed accordingly.

If you have any further questions in the meantime, please don't hesitate to reach out.

subject: Follow Up Questions
body:
Hi Sydney,

I hope you're doing well, and I apologize for the delayed response.

I'm glad to hear that. To address your question, you can extend your license at any time, and this will not affect your study at all. We will issue a new invoice for each extension. The only consideration is that the cost per participant per week is not fixed and is more efficient for larger projects compared to smaller ones. For instance, if you extend your license by 1 month for the 8 participants, the cost will be USD 117.26, which is the minimum fee. However, if you extend your license for another 3 months for the same number of participants, the cost will be USD 243.91. Similarly, if you want to add participants later, we’ll need to recalculate the cost for the additional participants. It would be more cost-effective to obtain a larger license now, if possible.

We can certainly ensure that the 3-month windows don't start until participants are added to the study. We will set the license period precisely as you want.

On another note, I want to let you know that our team has informed me that we might not be able to work on the "Clock Format Consistency" and "Text Formatting" options in the near future due to our busy schedule. Therefore, we might only be able to deliver these features by March next year or possibly later. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

If you have any more questions or need further details, please feel free to reach out.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara,
 
The ID of our study is 4065, you are correct.
 
The start and end dates for the study are currently tentative and flexible. Our proposed start date is November 18th, but we may need to adjust this if necessary. We plan to pause the study three months later, on February 18th, and will not be sending surveys to participants during this one-month pause. However, we will need access to our data during this time. If there is an additional cost for this access, please include it in the quote or invoice. After the pause, we intend to resume the study for a second phase with eight participants, which is expected to last another three months. This phase is likely to begin in early to mid-March and continue through June. I hope this information is sufficient for now!
 
We don't currently have an abstract to share, but here is a brief description: It remains unknown how the brain stores real-life emotional memories with their temporal context, and whether the fidelity of neural timestamps stored with individual emotional memories promote adaptive emotional recovery and regulation. The Life of Memories (LiMe) project will be the first deep-sampling study of real-life emotional memories, their neural underpinnings, and their emotional fate.
 
Looking forward to securing the license!
 
Best,
Sydney

subject: Follow Up Questions
body:
Hi Sydney,

I hope you are doing well. I apologize for the delay in my response; it’s been a busy week.

Thank you very much for sharing the details about your study. We look forward to collaborating on your project.

Generally speaking, included in the license cost, we maintain and store study data for 1 year free of charge, but anything further, will add 20% per year to the license cost. Please note that you will need to extend your license if the total duration of your study exceeds one year. We will set your license period from November 18, 2024, to November 18, 2025. Once you have more specific dates or updates, don’t hesitate to reach out, and we can adjust the plans accordingly.

  7. Annual Plan Quote: Finally, we would appreciate an updated quote for the annual plan if we aim to run approximately 60 participants and administer up to six surveys simultaneously.
That's all for now and please let us know if anything is unclear!

Best,
Nadu, Sydney and Mengsi

Dear Amin,

Thanks for coming to Santa Barbara to show us the app! It was really informative and helpful for us in our process of launching our first experience sampling study.
We have a few follow-up questions/requests on topics we touched on at the meeting. Specifically, we would like to kindly ask for clarification on which of these requests can be incorporated as part of the app's basic features (at no additional cost) and which would require a custom modification. For the latter, it would be helpful to receive an estimated timeline and cost for implementation.
  1. Batch Image Downloading: As we discussed, the ability to batch download images is crucial for us, as it would allow us to download and check the images in a timely manner and create follow up tests using them. You mentioned the possibility of providing a web scraping script that could automate downloading photos from the CSV file links. We believe this feature would benefit not only us but other users as well, so we kindly ask if this could be added as a core feature of the app. We would appreciate making this a priority, as we want to test the script soon and incorporate it into our data processing pipeline.
  2. Autocorrect for Text Responses: We are interested in exploring the possibility of adding an autocorrect function for text-based response questions. Could you provide us with a quote for implementing this feature and an estimate of how long it might take to integrate?
  3. Clock Format Consistency: Mengsi noticed a potential issue with time-based data collection, where the responses were recorded in a 24-hour format despite her input being in a 12-hour AM/PM format (likely due to her phone’s settings). We would like the time data input and output to be formatted consistently, regardless of participants’ device settings to avoid confusion. Is this something that could be addressed?
  4. Text Formatting Options: Some of our questions include long descriptions, and while we don't want them displayed in full every time, we’d like participants to be able to access them easily when needed. Is there a way to create collapsible/foldable text, where the full description is revealed upon clicking? Additionally, could we customize font size, style, and color etc to improve readability and reduce participants' cognitive load? We believe these features will also be beneficial for other users!
  5. Metadata Labels: We noticed that some of the metadata output contains numeric values for e.g. status and unanswered IDs, which we were unable to identify during the meeting. Could you clarify what labels or information are associated with these numbers?

  7. Annual Plan Quote: Finally, we would appreciate an updated quote for the annual plan if we aim to run approximately 60 participants and administer up to six surveys simultaneously.
That's all for now and please let us know if anything is unclear!

Best,
Nadu, Sydney and Mengsi

subject: Re: Follow Up Questions
body:
Hi Sara,
 
You are right - when I log in I can see the images.
 
About the web scraping script: could you ensure that after the images are all collected from the URL that each image is named with this naming convention: participantNumber_Daily_Survey_month_day_year_time_question
 
Here is an example (this was from a different experience sampling app that had a media download section): P6_Daily_Survey_08_05_2024_10-54 PM_neg1
 
Daily_Survey is the name of the survey - it should be consistent across participants, but the other parts of the filename should link up with each participant's details. So if the participant's Avicenna id is something like 12345 - that will always be shown as P12345 in that participant's image files. The date should always reflect the date that they took the survey, etc. Our survey has 4 image questions: neg1_image, neg2_image, pos1_image, pos2_image - so the script should be able to locate those files according to that column name (and just call it neg1, without the extra "_image" ). I attached an example of our data from our free trial so you can see the column names.
 
This naming convention makes it easy to link back each photo to the exact participant, question and day and time they took the survey. The images are a crucial component of our study so we want to make sure we can link back each unique image to the other info from the survey since we ask questions about how they felt about that exact experience (the experience captured in the image).
 
Could you please confirm that the web scraping script can have this? Thank you!
 
Best,
Nadu

Daily_Survey is the name of the survey - it should be consistent across participants, but the other parts of the filename should link up with each participant's details. The date should always reflect the date that they took the survey, etc. Our survey has 4 image questions: neg1_image, neg2_image, pos1_image, pos2_image - so the script should be able to locate those files according to that column name (and just call it neg1, without the extra "_image" ). I attached an example of our data from our free trial so you can see the column names.
This naming convention makes it easy to link back each photo to the exact participant, question and day and time they took the survey. The images are a crucial component of our study so we want to make sure we can link back each unique image to the other info from the survey since we ask questions about how they felt about that exact experience (the experience captured in the image).

Dear Amin,

Thanks for coming to Santa Barbara to show us the app! It was really informative and helpful for us in our process of launching our first experience sampling study.
We have a few follow-up questions/requests on topics we touched on at the meeting. Specifically, we would like to kindly ask for clarification on which of these requests can be incorporated as part of the app's basic features (at no additional cost) and which would require a custom modification. For the latter, it would be helpful to receive an estimated timeline and cost for implementation.
  1. Batch Image Downloading: As we discussed, the ability to batch download images is crucial for us, as it would allow us to download and check the images in a timely manner and create follow up tests using them. You mentioned the possibility of providing a web scraping script that could automate downloading photos from the CSV file links. We believe this feature would benefit not only us but other users as well, so we kindly ask if this could be added as a core feature of the app. We would appreciate making this a priority, as we want to test the script soon and incorporate it into our data processing pipeline.
  2. Autocorrect for Text Responses: We are interested in exploring the possibility of adding an autocorrect function for text-based response questions. Could you provide us with a quote for implementing this feature and an estimate of how long it might take to integrate?
  3. Clock Format Consistency: Mengsi noticed a potential issue with time-based data collection, where the responses were recorded in a 24-hour format despite her input being in a 12-hour AM/PM format (likely due to her phone’s settings). We would like the time data input and output to be formatted consistently, regardless of participants’ device settings to avoid confusion. Is this something that could be addressed?
  4. Text Formatting Options: Some of our questions include long descriptions, and while we don't want them displayed in full every time, we’d like participants to be able to access them easily when needed. Is there a way to create collapsible/foldable text, where the full description is revealed upon clicking? Additionally, could we customize font size, style, and color etc to improve readability and reduce participants' cognitive load? We believe these features will also be beneficial for other users!
  5. Metadata Labels: We noticed that some of the metadata output contains numeric values for e.g. status and unanswered IDs, which we were unable to identify during the meeting. Could you clarify what labels or information are associated with these numbers?
  6. FAQ Page: We briefly mentioned the creation of an FAQ page but didn’t get into specifics. Could you let us know what resources or tools are available to help us build this feature within the app?
  7. Annual Plan Quote: Finally, we would appreciate an updated quote for the annual plan if we aim to run approximately 60 participants and administer up to six surveys simultaneously.
That's all for now and please let us know if anything is unclear!

Best,
Nadu, Sydney and Mengsi

Batch Image Downloading: As we discussed, the ability to batch download images is crucial for us, as it would allow us to download and check the images in a timely manner and create follow up tests using them. You mentioned the possibility of providing a web scraping script that could automate downloading photos from the CSV file links. We believe this feature would benefit not only us but other users as well, so we kindly ask if this could be added as a core feature of the app. We would appreciate making this a priority, as we want to test the script soon and incorporate it into our data processing pipeline.
  2. Autocorrect for Text Responses: We are interested in exploring the possibility of adding an autocorrect function for text-based response questions. Could you provide us with a quote for implementing this feature and an estimate of how long it might take to integrate?
  3. Clock Format Consistency: Mengsi noticed a potential issue with time-based data collection, where the responses were recorded in a 24-hour format despite her input being in a 12-hour AM/PM format (likely due to her phone’s settings). We would like the time data input and output to be formatted consistently, regardless of participants’ device settings to avoid confusion. Is this something that could be addressed?
  4. Text Formatting Options: Some of our questions include long descriptions, and while we don't want them displayed in full every time, we’d like participants to be able to access them easily when needed. Is there a way to create collapsible/foldable text, where the full description is revealed upon clicking? Additionally, could we customize font size, style, and color etc to improve readability and reduce participants' cognitive load? We believe these features will also be beneficial for other users!
  5. Metadata Labels: We noticed that some of the metadata output contains numeric values for e.g. status and unanswered IDs, which we were unable to identify during the meeting. Could you clarify what labels or information are associated with these numbers?
  6. FAQ Page: We briefly mentioned the creation of an FAQ page but didn’t get into specifics. Could you let us know what resources or tools are available to help us build this feature within the app?
  7. Annual Plan Quote: Finally, we would appreciate an updated quote for the annual plan if we aim to run approximately 60 participants and administer up to six surveys simultaneously.
That's all for now and please let us know if anything is unclear!

Best,
Nadu, Sydney and Mengsi
